standard_prerequisites.name: Free system on finitely many generators
standard_prerequisites.statement: F_n is freely generated by a set of n elements, so its generated subsystems correspond to subsets of the free base.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the object of the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: Elementary embedding
standard_prerequisites.statement: An embedding preserving the truth of all formulas with parameters.

standard_prerequisites.name: Surjective endomorphism is an automorphism
standard_prerequisites.statement: Every surjective homomorphism of F_n onto itself is an automorphism.
standard_prerequisites.use: It converts surjectivity into the automorphism conclusion.

core_obligations: Write the free system with its free base and its image under the embedding, and use the elementarity to compare the generated subsystems (source line 1078).
Show that the image generates the whole system, which gives surjectivity; then invoke the cited remark to obtain that the embedding is an automorphism (source lines 1078-1085).

proof_roadmap.step: Compare the free base with its image through elementarity.
Conclude surjectivity and apply the surjective-endomorphism remark.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled proposition at source lines 1076-1077: for n at least three, every elementary embedding of the free system on n generators into itself is surjective, hence an automorphism. The proof (source lines 1078-1085) works with an explicit free base and its image, and the content is the comparison of the generated subsystems that elementarity permits; surjectivity follows once the image is seen to generate the whole system, and the automorphism conclusion is then read off the cited remark that surjective endomorphisms of the free system are automorphisms. The statement records the surjectivity and neither the comparison of generated subsystems nor the passage to automorphisms.
